thesis: Dysfunction of the somatostatin system is a shared feature of several neurodegenerative diseases and is probably causally involved in Alzheimer's disease; shared selective death of SST interneurons across neurodegenerative disease is not established. The distinction is not semantic - it determines whether the therapeutic target is a lost cell population to be replaced or a degraded signalling system to be restored.
scope_notes: Written last (Phase 11) and may cite only existing papers. Synthesizes the thesis answer and sets priorities for future work.

findings.claim: One hour of 40 Hz visual flicker lowered soluble Abeta40 and Abeta42 in visual cortex of 5XFAD mice by ~58% relative to dark controls, and optogenetic drive of fast-spiking PV interneurons at 40 Hz produced comparable CA1 reductions.

findings.evidence: Results: ELISA quantification of soluble Abeta after 1 h non-invasive 40 Hz light flicker in 5XFAD mice; parallel optogenetic FS-PV stimulation experiment in CA1. Two laboratories with different senior authors independently report reduced brain Abeta after 40 Hz stimulation in mouse models — one using visual flicker, one using vibrotactile delivery — so the modality differs in the second case while the measured effect matches.

findings.claim: Low-dose levetiracetam normalized hippocampal hyperactivity in amnestic mild cognitive impairment, bringing task-related activation to the level of age-matched controls and reducing DG/CA3-dependent memory errors.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Treatment with low dose levetiracetam significantly reduced that excess activity, such that hippocampal activation in patients on drug did not differ from age-matched control subjects.
findings.evidence: Results: fMRI during a mnemonic discrimination task, within-subject placebo-controlled crossover in aMCI patients. n refers to the 17 aMCI patients with complete usable data included in the analysis; 23 were enrolled and 6 were excluded for incomplete MRI, non-adherence or inability to complete. Replication is claimed only at the level of the shared measured outcome — levetiracetam-associated memory improvement in a hyperexcitable system — demonstrated by two laboratories with different senior authors in different species; the imaging and EEG endpoints themselves are not common to both. One convergent study from a laboratory with a different senior author (10.1073/pnas.1121081109) reports levetiracetam-associated memory improvement in a hyperexcitable system, but only one such study was identified, below the two-independent-source threshold required for an independently_replicated designation.

findings.claim: Human studies of neuronal resilience to Alzheimer's pathology rest on very small pathology-matched subgroups, with as few as six brains per category after Braak, CERAD and clinical matching, which limits replication of cell-type-specific resilience claims.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Brains from age- and sex-matched de-identified individuals were classified into AD (Braak V-VI, CERAD “Moderate” or “Frequent”, and a clinical diagnosis of AD dementia; n = 6), Resilient (Braak V-VI, CERAD “Moderate”, and clinical records of absence of cognitive impairment; n = 4), and Control (Braak 0-I, CERAD “None” or “Sparse”, and clinical records of absence of cognitive impairment; n = 6).
findings.evidence: Cases were stratified by amyloid, tangle burden and cognitive status before cell-type-resolved expression analysis; the stratification that makes the comparison interpretable is also what reduces each group to single-digit n.

findings.claim: In human hippocampus and temporal cortex somatostatin and neuropeptide Y are frequently co-expressed in the same neurons, so the two peptides index overlapping cell populations and their divergent behaviour in disease must reflect differential peptide regulation rather than differential cell survival.

arg_conflict_cluster_10_conf_08.thesis: Whether the somatostatin system is lost in human Alzheimer cortex. Marker-based cell counts report preferential loss of SST-immunoreactive cells, whereas direct peptidomic measurement finds SST-14 peptide preserved in pathology-matched resilient cases. The two measurements differ in modality (immunoreactive cell counts versus peptide quantification) and in cohort stratification (diagnosis versus cognition at matched pathology).
arg_conflict_cluster_10_conf_08.synthesis: Conflict cluster_10_conf_08 (foreground; resolution_status=unresolved). This section is the home of the cross-cutting methodological conflicts; all nine are argued explicitly. Primary axis (rule-derived, provisional): measurement_modality_and_what_was_counted.

arg_conflict_cluster_03_conf_03.thesis: Whether SST interneurons are the most vulnerable or a selectively preserved population in AD cortex. Deconvolution of bulk and single-nucleus data reports SST interneuron proportions as the cell type most reduced in AD, whereas the resilience-focused single-nucleus study describes SST+ interneurons as selectively preserved and protective. The dimension is cell-type vulnerability versus resilience, with different comparison groups (AD vs control vs cognitively resilient donors).
arg_conflict_cluster_03_conf_03.synthesis: Conflict cluster_03_conf_03 (foreground; resolution_status=open). SST interneurons reported as the most depleted cell type and as selectively preserved, from similar human data types. Primary axis (rule-derived, provisional): design_rigor_and_statistical_unit.

arg_conflict_cluster_09_conf_03.thesis: Magnitude and translation of 40 Hz entrainment benefit. Mouse studies report ~58% reductions in soluble Abeta after a single hour of flicker, whereas clinical gamma stimulation protocols of up to four weeks show no significant global cognitive improvement. The dimension of disagreement is species and endpoint (molecular amyloid load in mouse cortex versus global cognition in patients), with delivery modality also differing (sensory flicker versus transcranial alternating current).
arg_conflict_cluster_09_conf_03.synthesis: Conflict cluster_09_conf_03 (foreground; resolution_status=open). Magnitude and translation of the 40 Hz benefit - mouse molecular endpoints against patient cognition. Primary axis (rule-derived, provisional): species_region_and_circuit_context.

arg_unanchored.thesis: Dysfunction of the somatostatin system is a shared feature of several neurodegenerative diseases and is probably causally involved in Alzheimer's disease; shared selective death of SST interneurons across neurodegenerative disease is not established. The distinction is not semantic - it determines whether the therapeutic target is a lost cell population to be replaced or a degraded signalling system to be restored.
arg_unanchored.synthesis: 25 of 28 papers in this package are not tied to a named figure comparison or a recorded conflict. They are the synthesis density of the section: group them into convergent paragraphs of 5-8 citations each, giving landmark papers (argument_role=landmark) detailed treatment and the rest integrated as converging evidence. Do not cover them sequentially.

End on the conditional answer recorded in the scaffold's act_3 resolution: The thesis question is answered conditionally: SST interneuron dysfunction is a shared and probably causally contributing feature of AD and of circuit-level dysfunction in several other conditions, but "shared selective loss of the SST cell class across neurodegenerative disease" is not established, and the decisive experiments - marker-independent human counting, SST-selective manipulation inside a disease model, a prospective CSF somatostatin study with discrimination statistics - have not been done. Set priorities for future work; introduce no citation that is not already used in a body section.
framing_limits: May cite only papers already cited in body sections.
Must not introduce a claim stronger than the body sections support, and must restate the coverage limits once in plain terms.

certified_evidence_limits.search_coverage: Europe PMC-dominant retrieval. Endpoints actually used: Europe PMC REST search (resultType=core) and fullTextXML, NCBI E-utilities efetch (db=pmc), CrossRef. No other database contributed a comparable share, so coverage claims must be scoped to these sources.
certified_evidence_limits.citation_chasing: None. No backward or forward citation chasing was performed. No section may claim completeness of coverage; write 'no study examining X was retrieved by these searches', never 'no study has examined X'.
certified_evidence_limits.fulltext_shortfall_concentration: The shortfall is concentrated in pre-2000 closed-access postmortem and CSF literature (radioimmunoassay series), which is recorded at abstract level only. Sections whose argument rests on that literature must state the asymmetry in the section body, not only in Methods.
certified_evidence_limits.disconfirming_sweeps: Disconfirming-evidence sweeps were capped per query. Negative-result and conflict coverage is a top-relevance sample, not a census. Report null results as 'reported null results include ...'; never as 'no contradicting evidence exists'. No rate of contradiction may be reported as complete.
certified_evidence_limits.conflict_axis_labels_provisional: Axes were assigned by a documented rule applied to the recorded nature_of_conflict text. Five candidate axes (measurement modality and what was counted; species, region and circuit context; model construct and species transfer; cohort composition, stage and comorbidity; design rigor and statistical unit) were keyword-scored, with the region/species axis down-weighted (0.55) because regional context is named in almost every conflict record, and design rigor up-weighted (1.3) because it is named rarely and only when it is the point. Each conflict carries a primary axis and the full set of axes present, since most of these disagreements are genuinely multi-axis. These tags are a planning classification derived from the conflict text, not a measurement; the writing phase should correct any tag that misreads a conflict, and the atlas figure must state that conflicts can appear in more than one axis row.
certified_evidence_limits.conflict_inventory_caveat: This inventory is the set of disagreements recorded during a search whose disconfirming-evidence sweeps were capped per query. It is a top-relevance sample of the disagreement in this literature, not a census, and no rate of contradiction may be reported as complete.

scaffold_evidence_limits.limit: Europe PMC-dominant retrieval with no citation chasing (snowball_rounds = 0)
scaffold_evidence_limits.consequence_for_scaffold: No section may claim completeness of coverage. The Methods section states the database scope and the absence of backward/forward citation chasing explicitly. Claims of the form "no study has examined X" are written as "no study examining X was retrieved by these searches", and every such statement in a body section is sourced to a recorded evidence gap rather than asserted.

scaffold_evidence_limits.limit: Full-text share varies from 77/77 (circuits, cluster_07) to 22/87 (human evidence, cluster_08) because the older postmortem and CSF literature is closed-access
scaffold_evidence_limits.consequence_for_scaffold: Section 9 is the section whose underlying literature is least directly verified. Its thesis is written so that the central synthesis rests on the modern open-access single-nucleus cohorts, with the 1980s radioimmunoassay series treated as a historically important but abstract-level record; the asymmetry is stated in the section itself, not buried in Methods. Section 5 (25/80 full text) carries the same caveat for its historical CSF series.

scaffold_evidence_limits.limit: Disconfirming-evidence sweeps were capped per query, so negative-result coverage is a top-relevance sample rather than an exhaustive search
scaffold_evidence_limits.consequence_for_scaffold: Null results are reported as "reported null results include ..." and never as "no contradicting evidence exists". Section 11 states that the conflict inventory is a sample of the disagreement in this literature, not a census, and that the true rate of unreplicated or contradicted claims is bounded below by what is recorded here.

scaffold_evidence_limits.limit: cluster_09's replication ceiling (therapeutics) is met by a single enabling label; 60 of 86 findings are replication_unknown
scaffold_evidence_limits.consequence_for_scaffold: Section 10 is framed as an assessment of translational status, not of efficacy. No therapeutic claim in that section may be described as replicated unless the specific replicating DOI is named, and the section foregrounds that much of the SSTR4 evidence base comes from one closely related research programme.

scaffold_evidence_limits.limit: Figure comparisons are heterogeneous: no figure_data entry is uniform on all four homogeneity_check fields
scaffold_evidence_limits.consequence_for_scaffold: Every figure specification states the heterogeneity it must display rather than smooth, and the document-level figure rules forbid pooled summaries outright.

scaffold_evidence_limits.limit: Several prominent mechanistic claims are flagged as false-consensus risks in the evidence record (metabolic load as the cause of SST vulnerability; SST/GABA co-transmission; absolute sparing of striatal interneurons in HD)
scaffold_evidence_limits.consequence_for_scaffold: Each is introduced in prose as a widely repeated claim whose primary demonstration was not retrieved, in sections 3, 2 and 6 respectively, and each is listed in the section 11 open-questions inventory.

suggested_paragraph_groupings.topic: The answer to the question, stated conditionally
suggested_paragraph_groupings.what_binds_them: Answer each clause of the thesis question with the evidence tier attached: reproducible marker reduction (strong), early proportional depletion of SST neurons in human AD cortex (strong, cohort-based, annotation-dependent), cell-intrinsic vulnerability mechanisms (weak, largely inferred), peptide/SSTR signalling as a causal route to amyloid (contested, directly disputed), circuit consequences (strong in healthy animals, extrapolated to disease), biomarker status (not supported), therapeutic status (not demonstrated for the SST class).

suggested_paragraph_groupings.topic: What the field should stop doing
suggested_paragraph_groupings.what_binds_them: Three concrete practices: reporting marker counts as cell loss; pooling heterogeneous magnitudes into a consensus effect size; and treating convergence within one research programme as replication.

suggested_paragraph_groupings.topic: The experiments that would change the answer
suggested_paragraph_groupings.what_binds_them: Rank the decisive experiments and state what each would resolve, carrying the ranking from (sec-conflicts-limitations) and the therapeutic requirements from (sec-therapeutics).

Close on what is achievable with existing resources: marker-independent reanalysis of existing human cohorts, SST-selective manipulation in an established disease model, and a prospective fluid study designed as a diagnostic-accuracy study rather than a group comparison.

suggested_paragraph_groupings.what_explains_the_discrepancy: Whether the somatostatin system is lost in human Alzheimer cortex. Marker-based cell counts report preferential loss of SST-immunoreactive cells, whereas direct peptidomic measurement finds SST-14 peptide preserved in pathology-matched resilient cases. The two measurements differ in modality (immunoreactive cell counts versus peptide quantification) and in cohort stratification (diagnosis versus cognition at matched pathology).

Whether SST interneurons are the most vulnerable or a selectively preserved population in AD cortex. Deconvolution of bulk and single-nucleus data reports SST interneuron proportions as the cell type most reduced in AD, whereas the resilience-focused single-nucleus study describes SST+ interneurons as selectively preserved and protective. The dimension is cell-type vulnerability versus resilience, with different comparison groups (AD vs control vs cognitively resilient donors).

Magnitude and translation of 40 Hz entrainment benefit. Mouse studies report ~58% reductions in soluble Abeta after a single hour of flicker, whereas clinical gamma stimulation protocols of up to four weeks show no significant global cognitive improvement. The dimension of disagreement is species and endpoint (molecular amyloid load in mouse cortex versus global cognition in patients), with delivery modality also differing (sensory flicker versus transcranial alternating current).

suggested_paragraph_groupings.what_binds_them: Not tied to a named figure comparison or a recorded conflict; group into convergent paragraphs of 5-8 citations each rather than covering sequentially.

curation_notes.assignment_rule: Deterministic cluster->section mapping from gate_scope.json cluster_to_section_assignment, applied to unique (doi, claim_source_sentence) evidence units.
curation_notes.bookend_rule: Sections 01 and 12 are bookends written at Phase 11 and may cite only papers already used in body sections. Each bookend finding is a Phase 2 finding whose DOI also carries a different finding, with a different claim_source_sentence, in a body section - so the paper is already in the body and the two sections quote different sentences.
curation_notes.duplicate_policy: 35 of 844 Phase 2 findings were byte-identical (same DOI and same claim_source_sentence) records of the same observation in two or more clusters. They were merged into the surviving finding object (also_recorded_in_clusters / duplicate_finding_ids_merged) and logged in unassigned_findings.json; none were deleted.
curation_notes.conflict_axis_caveat: AXIS labels on conflicts are rule-derived and provisional (scaffold conflict_coverage.axis_assignment_method). Correct any tag that misreads a conflict.
curation_notes.citation_discipline: Papers in this package come only from Phase 2 outputs. Do not introduce new citations; cite_keys are from the certified citation_key_map and author names only from author_name_table.
